newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Regrade in on firm gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Regrade in on firm gas oil.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade narrowed at midday on Friday after large increases to gas oil values over the week with the jet fuel fundamentals seen unchanged, traders said.
"The regrade took a hit after the big gains on gas oil because the jet fuel fundamentals have not changed," one trader said.
The August regrade was last quoted at $1.25/$1.40 per barrel from Thursday's $1.40/$1.50, brokers said. August traded on late Thursday at $1.45 and $1.35 per barrel, they said.
The prices are well off the $1.80/$2.00 quoted on Monday.
Although the regrade has narrowed sharply, outright jet fuel prices have risen on the back of the sharp increase in gas oil prices. But the gas oil price rise has been relatively bigger.
Several sellers took advantage of the latest rally and came out to offer a total of five jet cargoes late Thursday with the lowest at $24.50 per barrel for August 8-12 lifting.
But no firm buying interest was seen and most traders said that there was no reason to pay the higher prices for jet fuel simply off the back of firmer gas oil.
Physical jet fuel last traded on Tuesday at $23.40.
Jet fuel's rise is due to the more than $1.50 per barrel rise of gas oil in just one week, which still leaves many players puzzled.
August swaps were last quoted at $23.10/$23.25 per barrel, almost unchanged from Thursday's $23.10/$22.20 per barrel, brokers said.
August traded to a high of $23.50 on Thursday compared to a traded low of $21.50 on Friday.
The surge in the front month has narrowed the August/September contango to value at about minus 40 cents from its last traded level of minus 44 cents, brokers said.

The swaps strength was perpetuated in the physical market late Thursday when a Dutch trader bought a 150,000-barrel cargo from a European major at $22.75 per barrel, up 85 cents from Wednesday's traded high of $21.90 and $1.45 more than the day-earlier traded low of $21.30.
August fuel oil midday Friday was quoted at $99.50/$100.00 per tonne, up 50 cents from Thursday after values rose on firm bids late Thursday.
